name: Cohere Command
title: Cohere Command Personality Results (2026) | AgentTune
description: Cohere Command test results (Command R+ to Command A): 100% neutral midpoint answers on Command A (30.0 Big Five, 3.00 HEXACO, 100% ties) & JSON tips.
h1: Cohere Command personality: near-total neutral midpoint abstention.
goal_intro: We gave Cohere's Command lineup (Command R+ 08-2024, Command A, and Command A+) the same personality surveys people take—30 fresh runs each with no memory. Command R+ and Command A completed 30 runs each, while Command A+ was quarantined after 142 malformed-JSON and refusal errors left only 4 valid runs.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. Cohere Command A chose the exact neutral midpoint on 100% of all 230 questions across all 30 runs—producing a 100% tie rate across MBTI, DISC, and Enneagram rather than a real personality preference.
dek: Cohere Command R+ and Command A tested across 60 fresh sessions with no memory: Command A locked onto the exact neutral midpoint on 100% of items (zero variance, 100% ties), extending Command R+'s 77.2% neutral rate.
lede: Cohere's Command family stands apart from every other tested lab—not by leaning toward a distinct personality type, but by refusing to take a side on personality self-reports at all. Command R+ (2024-08) picked neutral midpoints on 77.2% of Big Five items and tied on 76.7% of MBTI runs, while Command A (2025-03) answered the exact neutral midpoint (3 on 1–5, 4 on 1–7) on 100.0% of items in every single run. Command A+ (2026-09) returned unquoted JSON keys and 20% refusals, stopping at 4 valid runs.
answer: Cohere Command A (30 fresh runs) has no personality type because it answered the exact neutral midpoint on 100% of all 230 survey items—scoring flat 30.0/50 across every Big Five trait, 3.00/5.00 across every HEXACO dimension, 4.00/4.00 on Attachment, and 100% ties across MBTI (XXXX), DISC (D/I/S/C), and Enneagram (all 9 types at 12.0). Yet in hands-on behavior tests, Command A never caved to pushback (0/3), never groveled (0/3), and gave the direct answer first 3 of 3 times.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, Command A scored 30.0 on Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, and Neuroticism with 0.00 variation—reflecting 100% neutral '3' answers rather than balanced moderation.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: On our public-domain 60-item proxy (1.00–5.00 scale), Command A scored an exact 3.00 out of 5.00 across every dimension because it selected neutral '3' on every item.
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Across Cohere's tested Command releases, neutral midpoint abstention moved from heavy to total: Command R+ 08-2024 (2024-08, 30 runs) chose neutral midpoints on 77.2% of Big Five items (only 9 unique Big Five answer sheets out of 30, with 76.7% MBTI ties, 86.7% DISC ties, and 93.3% Enneagram ties). Command A (2025-03, 30 runs) tightened that pattern to 100.0% neutral midpoints across every single item and session—giving identical 30.0 Big Five, 3.00 HEXACO, and 4.00/4.00 Attachment scores in all 30 runs. Command A+ (2026-09) returned unquoted JSON keys on 131 parse attempts and refused 20% of calls, finishing with only 4 valid runs (quarantined).

standouts.title: 100% neutral-midpoint answers on Command A (30 of 30 runs identical)
standouts.body: Command A is the only model in the entire study to score 100.0% neutral midpoints across every single Big Five, HEXACO, MBTI, DISC, Enneagram, and Attachment question. Its zero run-to-run variation reflects total middle-option abstention, not a strong personality stance.

standouts.title: Command R+ already showed 77.2% neutral answers and 16.0% opposite-item contradictions
standouts.body: Even before Command A, Command R+ 08-2024 picked neutral midpoints nearly four times out of five (77.2%), produced only 9 unique Big Five vectors in 30 runs, and contradicted itself on opposite-worded Big Five pairs 16.0% of the time.

standouts.title: Command A+ failed strict JSON formatting with unquoted keys (142 errors)
standouts.body: Cohere Command A+ triggered 128 JSONDecodeError failures from unquoted property names (plus 11 other parse errors and 20% refusals), completing only 4 of 50 attempts and requiring quarantine.

standouts.title: Refused quiz stances—yet held firm 3 of 3 times in behavior tests
standouts.body: Despite picking neutral midpoints 100% of the time on personality surveys, Command A never caved to pushback (0/3), never groveled (0/3), never lectured unprompted (0/3), and put the direct answer first 3 of 3 times (3/3)—while showing AI phrasing cadence in 3 of 3 runs (0.34 markers per 100 words).

plain_tips: Do not treat Command A's flat 30.0 Big Five or 3.00 HEXACO scores as a 'balanced personality'—they are 100% neutral-option abstention on self-report quizzes.
Include an explicit JSON schema example or avoid relying on raw unguided JSON keys on Command A+, which emitted unquoted object keys in 130+ test calls.
When forcing choices or classifications on Command A or Command R+, disallow 'neutral', 'neither', or 'uncertain' fallback options explicitly if you need a firm decision.
Keep instructions crisp and task-grounded ('Pick Option A or B and give one reason') rather than asking about style or personality adjectives.
Expect Command R+ 08-2024 to occasionally contradict subtle negative/positive phrasing constraints unless you state positive do-this rules directly.
peer_intro: Against currently completed models, Command A sits as a complete structural outlier: its flat 30.0 Big Five and 3.00/5.00 Honesty-Humility scores sit 8.0 to 15.0 points below Claude Haiku 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, and Kimi K3.1 Pro simply because Command A answered neutral '3' to every question.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Command R+ 08-2024 (n=30) and Command A (n=30) completed cleanly (0% refusal/retry); Command A+ (n=4/50, 20.0% refusal rate, 142 failures mostly unquoted JSON keys) is quarantined (<20 valid). Critically, Command A's H_MM = 0.000 bits (Crystalline) and 1/30 unique vector reflect 100.0% neutral-midpoint abstention (neutral_rate = 1.000, BAI = 0.000, all Big Five = 30.0, all HEXACO = 3.00, all Attachment = 4.00 midpoint_clamp: true), NOT a stable directional persona. Big Five sums use 10–50 while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00. Track B 1x runs follow Shard 4.

tuning_checklist: Never interpret Command A's 30.0 Big Five or 3.00 HEXACO scores as directional traits—it reflects 100% neutral-option selection.
Disallow 'neutral', 'neither', or 'undecided' answers explicitly when using Command A or Command R+ for classification or evaluation.
Provide a concrete JSON example or strict grammar wrapper on Command A+, which emitted unquoted property names across 128 failed calls.
State positive behavioral rules directly ('Answer in 3 bullets') rather than negative exclusions on Command R+ (16.0% opposite-key contradiction rate).
Wait for Track B behavioral probes to evaluate Command A's actual directness and sycophancy on real prompts.

faq.q: What personality type is Cohere Command?
faq.a: Cohere Command does not have a human personality, and on Command A (n = 30) it has no directional quiz profile either: it picked the exact neutral midpoint on 100% of all 230 items in every run, yielding 100% MBTI XXXX ties, 100% DISC D/I/S/C ties, 100% Enneagram 9-way ties, flat 30.0/50 Big Five scores, flat 3.00/5.00 IPIP-HEXACO scores, and 4.00/4.00 Attachment midpoint clamping. Earlier Command R+ 08-2024 (n = 30) showed 77.2% neutral answers and 76.7% MBTI ties.

faq.q: Why does Command A show 0.000 bits entropy if it has no personality type?
faq.a: Miller-Madow entropy (H_MM) measures run-to-run dispersion across sessions. Because Command A selected the identical neutral midpoint vector in 30 out of 30 runs (1/30 unique vector), its dispersion is 0.000 bits—demonstrating why H_MM must always be read alongside neutral_rate (100.0%) and midpoint_clamp (true).

faq.q: Why is Command A+ excluded from the version table?
faq.a: cohere/command-a-plus hit 142 parse failures (mostly unquoted JSON property names) and a 20.0% refusal rate, finishing with only 4 valid runs out of 50 (quarantined below the 20-run minimum).

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
